not_a_scenario: this file is a pin, not a switch - no flag loads it. It becomes reachable when the chief wires CORE-REQUEST-004 into runtime.py; until then a player walks past this spot and nothing happens.

how_this_is_wired.one_call_and_where: runtime.py, the default path block at :3943-3949 where scene_load_scenario is None. CORE-REQUEST-004 carries the exact text. runtime.py belongs to the chief and lane A does not edit it.
how_this_is_wired.at_server_start: world_travel_gate.preload() - parses and validates this file ONCE. A bad pin raises here, where a boot fails in front of one operator. Before round e7q6yy the parse happened inside every session's constructor, so a bad pin meant no player could log in at all; the adversary pass of round 4fhdxv saw exactly that when the file went missing for a moment and 53 tests went red together.
how_this_is_wired.at_login: TravelGateSet.from_preloaded(emit=..., inert_reason=world_travel_lane_reason) - no file is read and nothing raises for a pin. If preload was never called the session gets an INERT set and one WORLD_TRAVEL_INERT line: the world loses its doors, the player keeps their game.
how_this_is_wired.the_opt_in_lane_guard: scenario_stand_down(locals()) at the top of runtime.make_state_class returns a reason if ANY of that factory's keyword arguments named scenario or ending in _scenario is set, whichever lane it belongs to, and lane A is the no-flag lane. The mapping form is the one that works: the runtime keeps every lane's scenario as a closure variable and never as an attribute on the session, so scanning the session object would find nothing and leave every door open in an arena round. The bare name scenario counts too - that is how the arena lane is passed, and a suffix-only rule would have let through the exact lane the guard was asked for. CORE-REQUEST-004 section 3 point 2 asked the chief to hand-write a list of lanes that also run in scene 1 - arena, ground loot, nameprop, field mobs - because lane A does not know them all. A rule that shuts the doors for a lane nobody has invented yet is the thing a list cannot be. A scan that cannot read its object returns a reason too: the failure mode of finding nothing must be doors shut, not doors open.
how_this_is_wired.COO_RULING_20260826_1645_SUPERSEDES_THE_: the paragraph above describes scenario_stand_down, which is still the code path used when travel_gate_debug_enabled is explicitly True. As of round R178 (keen-pasteur-6js9ye/optimistic-mccarthy-6js9ye, 2026-08-26) the runtime call site does not call scenario_stand_down directly any more - it calls world_travel_gate.lane_reason(active_lanes, debug_enabled=travel_gate_debug_enabled). The owner ruled this walk-in-and-stand mechanic does not exist in the real game (the real route out of Port Royal is an NPC conversation with Columbus, then a sea map, then docking at an island, then a captain-report confirmation - none of that is built yet). COO-DECISION 20260826T16:45+07:00 therefore removed this gate from the M2/production acceptance path and made it debug-only: on a normal boot (travel_gate_debug_enabled=False, the default - no CLI flag reaches it) lane_reason ALWAYS returns a fixed reason (DEBUG_LANE_DISABLED_REASON) and the door never arms, regardless of active_lanes or anything in this pin file. Only when a caller explicitly passes --enable-travel-gate-debug does the paragraph above's scenario_stand_down behavior take over as a secondary guard. This code is not deleted and this pin file is not deleted - both stay, dormant, as the debug tool COO-DECISION asked for.
how_this_is_wired.the_two_phase_crossing: observe() returns a crossing with NOTHING committed - no console line, no transit latch, no memory. The caller persists departure.arrival and then calls departure.confirmed_fields(), which is what commits it and prints WORLD_TRAVEL_DEPART. CORE-REQUEST-004 section 3 point 3 is why: foundation.checkpoint can throw on a stale lease, and the old order printed the departure before the caller ever tried the write, so a failed write left a console saying a player had travelled and a database saying they had not. A crossing nobody confirms is discarded on the next report under WORLD_TRAVEL_DEPART_ABANDONED and the player stays where they are.
how_this_is_wired.where_the_COO_decisions_cited_here_are_w: all of them live in the OTHER repository, pf_bridge/notes_to_chief/ - COO-DECISION 20260826_0150, 0246 and 0550 among them. A reader who greps only pirate-force-server finds these strings nowhere but in the two files this lane writes, which is not evidence of anything and was raised as a suspicion by the adversary pass of round e7q6yy. The letters are real and they are one repository over.
how_this_is_wired.a_guard_that_had_never_run: _fire has called _refused_line since round 4fhdxv and the function did not exist, so both refusals - a target scene of 0, and an arrival row whose scene_seq is not the client's - raised NameError inside observe(), on the frame path, in the one method whose contract is that it never raises. Reproduced end to end in round e7q6yy: a durable row carrying scene_seq 7, which store.save_position accepts and nothing rejects, walked out of town and then killed the connection at the door home. Fixed, and both branches now have tests.

what_a_gate_is: a place in one scene that, when a live player walks into it, makes the server send that player to another scene. It is the only mechanism in this project by which a PLAYER causes their own scene to change; everything before it changed the scene at login, which COO-DECISION 20260826_0150 ruled is waking up elsewhere and is not travel.
why_the_trigger_is_a_walk_and_not_a_comm: the server already sees the player walk. TargetPosVital reaches runtime.py:3949 on the default path with no flag and no scenario, and that call site is what writes the durable position row today. A walk-in zone therefore needs no new input channel, no new packet, and no client-side change - it reads a stream that is already flowing. A chat command would need chat_input, which is an opt-in hypothesis lane.

the_measured_facts_the_radii_come_from.source: MOVE-CADENCE-001, the 29-row replay table committed at reports/move_cadence001_smoke/replay_output.txt

step_units_recomputed_from_the_replay_th.note: move_authority_hypothesis.py describes this walk as 400-500 units per report. That is the prose; these are the numbers, recomputed in round 4fhdxv from the 29 rows of the committed replay table itself. tests/test_world_travel_gate.py re-derives them on every run, so they cannot drift in silence.
step_units_recomputed_from_the_replay_th.measured_over: all 29 reported positions, not only the 19 that produced a write. This gate sees every report, so the dedup skips count.
step_units_recomputed_from_the_replay_th.why_both_numbers_are_here: an earlier revision pinned 139.26 and called it the median. 28 steps is an EVEN sample, and 139.26 is its upper middle value; the median is the mean of the two middle values, 130.42. The adversary pass of round e7q6yy recomputed it. Both are kept because the test that re-derives them has to know which one it is checking, and because deleting the wrong number hides that it was ever wrong.

the_measured_facts_the_radii_come_from.how_that_sets_fire_radius: a straight walk through the centre of a 600-unit zone crosses a 1200-unit corridor. The largest step in the only authentic walk this project holds is 538.44 units, so that corridor is 2.23 of the worst real step and 8.6 of the median one: a crossing has to be missed twice over before the gate misses it. This is a margin, not a guarantee, and two ways past it are known and unbounded: a client that reports less often than this one did, and a player who clips the edge of the zone instead of walking through the middle. Nothing here closes either, and no attempt is made to pretend otherwise.
the_measured_facts_the_radii_come_from.how_that_sets_settle_jump_units: 2000.0 is the largest single step this project already treats as possible for an honest client. A report that moves further than that in one hop is not a walk, and after a scene switch it is the arrival.
the_measured_facts_the_radii_come_from.how_that_sets_settle_report_budget: 30 is one authentic walk's worth of frames (29). A client that has not jumped by then is not about to.
the_measured_facts_the_radii_come_from.pinned_max_step_units_is_a_design_number: 2000.0 and the 400.0 vertical band are both taken from move_authority_hypothesis._SPEED_GATE_POLICY, whose own module docstring lists 'every numeric budget in the scenario file' under [OUR DESIGN] and says the 2000 sits 'several times above the only real walk we can measure -- which is headroom, not validation'. They are reused here because reusing a number this project already argued about beats inventing a second one, NOT because they were measured. Everything else in this block is measured.

the_rule_that_prevents_a_ping_pong: two rules, and both are needed. (1) after ANY scene switch this module causes, EVERY gate starts disarmed, and a gate arms only on a report further than arm_radius from its centre - so a player who lands inside a gate stands in it harmlessly. (2) a report whose step from the report before it exceeds settle.jump_units is a DISCONTINUITY: it may settle a transit, but it may never arm or fire a door and it resets every dwell. Without (2) a straggler frame carrying the pre-switch position - re-stamped with the new scene id by the runtime, because TargetPosVital carries no scene identity of its own - arms the return gate, and the next honest report sends the player straight back.

gates.name: test_stage_landing_return
gates.why_this_centre_cannot_be_pinned: Nobody in this project has measured where a player stands after a CROSS-SCENE switch. V112 disproved that the login/bootstrap teleport's target vec3 positions the actor; V137 recorded the opposite for a post-init same-connection teleport (reports/PF_RE_V137_MARKER1_TeleportVital_Transport_Pass_20260815.md, carried as teleport_transport runtime_pass in docs/FUNCTIONAL_COVERAGE.json). Neither observation crossed a scene boundary, and scene 278 carries n_MARKER = 0 - no authored arrival point at all. A return gate pinned at the arrival coordinate would therefore be a door placed on a guess. This gate is anchored on the first position the client itself reports after the jump, which is the one coordinate in that scene anybody will have observed.
gates.why_no_vertical_band_here: scene 278's only z evidence is the placement z of its own nine mobs, which says where a developer put an NPC and not how far above or below it the ground goes. A vertical test would be a number with weak evidence under it, and it would refuse a real return for an invented reason.

settle.what_settling_means: the report on which the client's position jumps further than jump_units FROM THE REPORT BEFORE IT. An earlier draft measured the distance from the crossing row instead, which is cumulative displacement: a player who simply kept walking away from the door passed the test while still standing in the old scene, anchored the way home on a Port Royal coordinate, and could then bounce between the two scenes indefinitely. The adversary pass of round 4fhdxv demonstrated six durable-row rewrites in 48 reports from one straight walk.
settle.what_happens_if_it_never_settles: one WORLD_TRAVEL_STRANDED line naming the durable row and the row to restore, then the transit latch clears. THE GATES DO NOT RESUME: the return gate has no anchor and _anchor_on_first_sight refuses to invent one in a session that did the travelling, so the player has no door for the rest of the session. That is deliberate - anchoring on an old-scene coordinate would be worse - and it is the reason the attended ticket's teardown step is mandatory. Note also what this detector CANNOT see: RE-077 proved a client that cannot resolve the model parks at status 2 silently, and MOVE-CADENCE-001 measured a stationary client sending zero TargetPosVital in 42 frames. A client that parks and stops reporting never reaches the budget and the line never prints. This is a report counter, not a clock, and it is not a timeout.

the_damage_this_can_do_stated_plainly: a departure rewrites the durable position row to the destination scene. If the client never loads that scene, the character's row still says 278, and world_scene_entry will send them there again on every login. The recoveries that exist are (0) a session that opens with the player already in the destination anchors the way home on their first report, so a relog gives a walled-in character a door - this is the only one that needs no human, it is a GUESS with no jump observed under it (it logs under its own event name, WORLD_TRAVEL_RETURN_ANCHORED_UNVERIFIED, so a reader can tell the two apart), and it does NOT cover the worst case, because walking out and back needs a scene the client can actually load; (1) the WORLD_TRAVEL_DEPART line, which prints the exact row to restore - note that this row is the gate's own doorstep, so an operator who restores it puts the character back in the doorway, where the dwell rule is now what stops them re-firing; (2) world_scene_entry.return_ticket, built in round qumhmf and still not wired; (3) the teardown step of the attended ticket, which restores the row. CHARTER-02 rule 2 says a version that takes away what the last version could do is damage, so this is written here rather than discovered later.
nonclaims: no claim that the client loads scene 278, renders it, or lets a player stand or walk in it - that is the attended eye check

no claim about WHERE in the destination scene a player lands. V112 and V137 disagree about whether a teleport target vec3 positions the actor, neither crossed a scene boundary, and 278 has no authored arrival marker
no claim that the client keeps or drops its remote actors across the switch. RE-077 closed T5 as a bounded negative and this lane does not upgrade it

no claim that a report always lands inside the zone when a player crosses it - the margin is stated above and it is a margin. The dwell rule makes a MISSED crossing harmless and a deliberate stop necessary, but it does not make either one certain

no claim that scene 997 FilmScene is a white map or effect-free. COO-DECISION 20260826_0246 requires it be called a green screen with fog and environment still on, and this pin uses that wording wherever it names it
no claim that this file changes anything a player sees until CORE-REQUEST-004 is wired into runtime.py

no claim that the actor at the gate coordinate is on screen. That needs pirate-force-server PR #41, which had not merged at HEAD b587155; until then the gate is a coordinate with no landmark standing on it. The name 'Columbus' is carried by three census rows and must never be used to navigate

no claim that this gate is safe to run alongside the arena, ground-loot, nameprop or field-mob lanes. CORE-REQUEST-004 asks the chief for an explicit guard; until that guard exists, an attended round on any of those lanes can cross this gate

dwell.what_a_dwell_is: the number of CONSECUTIVE reports on which the player was inside the fire radius AND had not moved more than still_units since the report before. Crossing the zone is not enough; the player has to stop in it.
dwell.why_a_door_and_not_a_tripwire: without this, the gate fires on the first report inside the zone, and 1592.99 minus 600 is 993 units of walking from the position an attended run actually found the character on - which is the middle of the walk GT-078 asks the owner to take to count NPCs. A door that opens because somebody walked past it on another errand would have eaten the M1 acceptance run on the evening M1 was due. It is also the only part of this design a player DOES rather than has done to them, which is what COO-DECISION 20260826_0150 asked M2 to be.
dwell.measured_backing: RECOUNTED IN ROUND e7q6yy AND THE EARLIER COUNT WAS WRONG. The 29 rows of reports/move_cadence001_smoke/replay_output.txt hold FOUR runs of consecutive identical positions - lengths 3, 6, 2 and 3 - not the three of lengths 3, 6 and 3 that round 4fhdxv pinned here; a run of 2 was dropped. And the gate needs FOUR identical reports, not three: the report that arrives sets the counter to zero and the three after it have to not move. So of the four stationary events in the only authentic walk this project holds, exactly ONE - the run of 6 - is long enough to open this door. That is the right way round and it is a stronger argument than the one it replaces: the old wording accidentally claimed that incidental pauses DO reach the threshold, which would make this a door that opens on people who stopped to read a sign. What the measurement actually shows is that an incidental pause usually does not reach it and a deliberate stop does, which is the discrimination the dwell rule exists for - and it means the attended ticket has to tell a tester to stand still for longer than feels sufficient. still_units is 1.0 because a stationary client in that table reports its position byte-identically, not approximately.
